---
title: "About"
---

**What this is.** The ACG Atlas is an index of research about the Área de Conservación Guanacaste, not a repository. It has two parts that are searched separately but share the same design: **data** (datasets in permanent archives) and **publications** (papers about research done in the ACG). It complements the ACG's own information systems by making both findable and citable in one place.

**How datasets get here.** A weekly harvest searches DataCite (which covers Dryad, Zenodo, EDI, Figshare, PANGAEA and more) and GBIF (spatially, by the ACG boundary), and researchers can submit DOIs on the [Contribute](contribute.qmd) page. Every entry is reviewed before it is published.

**How papers get here.** Papers are found by searching Web of Science and OpenAlex for ACG place names, then screened by title and abstract: a paper is included if the research was done in the ACG (any sector, including marine), uses ACG specimens or data, or is mainly about the ACG. Published records come from OpenAlex (CC0) or Crossref; no Web of Science records are republished. The weekly harvest adds new OpenAlex matches to the review queue, and anyone can suggest a paper we missed. The full search strategy is in [`data-raw/literature_search.md`](https://github.com/acg-atlas/acg-data-catalog/blob/main/data-raw/literature_search.md).

**Credit.** Each dataset and paper keeps its authors, license and citation. Please cite the original work, using its DOI.

**Map.** Occurrence density tiles from the GBIF maps API; basemaps from Esri. Density cells are not clipped to the ACG boundary.

**Boundary.** ACG boundary layer courtesy of SIG-ACG (Waldy Medina), CC BY 4.0.

**Coming next.** Links between papers and the datasets they use, tags for taxa and themes, and an evidence and gap map.

**Code.** All code and curation decisions are public at [github.com/acg-atlas](https://github.com/acg-atlas).
